question: Why can't you flatten a balloon without tearing or stretching it?
answer: A balloon's skin curves two ways at once, so laid flat it must split or stretch. Closing the gaps, as Mercator's map does, keeps shapes right but makes lands near the poles swell. No flat map of a round world is free of distortion.
move: No flat map of a round world is free of distortion.
